report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Fixed 20-week deadline and explicit team composition drive predictive structure; integration complexity with legacy/deprecated APIs and evolving requirements for lineage visualization require sprint-based refinement in Phases 2-3.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build a real-time monitoring platform surfacing pipeline health, data freshness, SLA breach alerts, and lineage visualization for ~400 active pipelines across Airflow, dbt, and Snowflake.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Data engineering team (12 engineers), data analysts, PMs, finance stakeholders.
project_understanding.trigger: Two production incidents in last quarter caused by undetected pipeline failures; VP of Data mandated solution before end of Q3.
success_definition: All pipeline failures detected within 5 minutes
SLA breach alerts sent to on-call within 2 minutes
Data lineage visible end-to-end for any dataset
Analyst self-service: no tickets to data engineering for data freshness queries
supporting_quotes: Two production incidents in the last quarter caused by undetected pipeline failures — one resulted in a missed board-level financial report
The Airflow metadata database is on a legacy version (1.10) with no official API — requires direct DB reads
The dbt integration relies on an undocumented internal API that the vendor has flagged for deprecation

assumption_log.what: Airflow 1.10 metadata DB direct read access is technically feasible and will not require schema reverse-engineering beyond Phase 1 discovery.
assumption_log.why: Legacy systems often have stable schemas; direct DB reads are a known pattern for unsupported APIs. However, this is a high-risk assumption given the age and lack of official support.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification before planning baseline.
assumption_log.consequence: If schema is undocumented or unstable, Phase 2 development will stall; data extraction logic will require extensive reverse-engineering and testing, adding 3-4 weeks to critical path.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning to proceed without vendor engagement delay. Risks: if schema is complex or unstable, timeline doubles for Airflow integration.

assumption_log.what: dbt vendor deprecation timeline is at least 6 months away (beyond project delivery), allowing Phase 2-3 integration to complete before API sunset.
assumption_log.why: Vendors typically provide 6-12 month deprecation windows. Input states 'next major release' without specifying when that occurs.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification before planning baseline.
assumption_log.consequence: If deprecation occurs during Phase 2-3, integration work must pivot to alternative API or workaround; 2-3 weeks of rework on critical path.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows dbt integration to proceed on current API. Risks: if deprecation is imminent, project must pivot mid-development.

assumption_log.what: Data lineage visualization scope is limited to pipeline-level lineage (which datasets feed which pipelines) rather than column-level lineage (which columns transform into which columns).
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'lineage visible end-to-end for any dataset' but does not define granularity. Column-level lineage is significantly more complex and would require data catalog integration.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted requirements.
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholders expect column-level lineage, Phase 2 scope expands by 4-6 weeks; requires data catalog integration (Collibra, Alation, or custom metadata layer).
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: delivers dataset-level lineage in 20 weeks. Risks: if column-level lineage is required, timeline extends beyond Q3 deadline.

assumption_log.what: Snowflake integration uses official Snowflake API and Python SDK; no direct database access required.
assumption_log.why: Snowflake provides well-documented, supported APIs. Input does not flag Snowflake as a constraint.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline derived from scope definition.
assumption_log.consequence: If Snowflake integration requires custom connectors or undocumented APIs, Phase 2 effort increases by 1-2 weeks.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Snowflake integration is straightforward. Risks: if custom connectors needed, timeline slips.

assumption_log.what: On-call alerting infrastructure (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or internal equivalent) already exists and is accessible via API; no build required.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'SLA breach alerts sent to on-call' but does not mention building alerting infrastructure. Mature data teams typically have on-call systems.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.4 — Scope baseline requires accepted requirements.
assumption_log.consequence: If on-call system does not exist or is not accessible, Phase 3 integration adds 2-3 weeks; requires separate alerting platform build.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: assumes alerting infrastructure exists. Risks: if it does not, scope expands significantly.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend engineers and data engineer must be dedicated full-time (80%+ allocation) to critical path; any part-time assignment or context-switching will cause schedule slip. DevOps engineer back-loaded to Phase 5 can be shared with other workstreams.

dbt API contract and deprecation timeline confirmed with vendor

tasks.name: Audit Airflow 1.10 metadata database schema and document pipeline state tables
tasks.definition_of_done: Schema documentation complete; sample queries tested against live Airflow DB; access credentials confirmed.

tasks.name: Confirm dbt API contract and deprecation timeline with vendor; document integration points
tasks.definition_of_done: Written confirmation from vendor on API stability and deprecation date; integration points documented.

tasks.name: Design monitoring platform architecture: ingestion, storage, query, alerting layers
tasks.definition_of_done: Architecture diagram approved by VP of Data; technology choices (time-series DB, message queue, alert routing) documented.

tasks.name: Define SLA thresholds and alert rules for 400 pipelines
tasks.definition_of_done: SLA matrix (by pipeline criticality) approved; alert rule templates defined.

tasks.name: Design data model for pipeline metadata, lineage, and freshness tracking
tasks.definition_of_done: ER diagram and schema DDL approved; lineage representation (DAG structure) documented.

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Airflow metadata ingestion pipeline running and validated
dbt integration extracting model metadata and lineage
Snowflake data freshness queries operational
Core monitoring backend API endpoints implemented
Internal demo: pipeline health dashboard showing live data

tasks.name: Build Airflow 1.10 metadata extraction connector using direct DB reads
tasks.definition_of_done: Connector extracts task state, run history, and failure logs; tested against live Airflow instance; handles schema edge cases.

tasks.name: Build dbt metadata and lineage extraction using vendor API
tasks.definition_of_done: Connector extracts dbt model metadata, lineage, and test results; handles API rate limiting and errors gracefully.

tasks.name: Build Snowflake data freshness query engine and metadata sync
tasks.definition_of_done: Queries return last-modified timestamp for all tracked datasets; sync runs every 5 minutes; latency < 30 seconds.

tasks.name: Implement message queue (Kafka/RabbitMQ) for pipeline event streaming
tasks.definition_of_done: Message queue receives pipeline state changes from all three sources; topics partitioned by pipeline; no message loss.

tasks.name: Build time-series database schema and ingestion pipeline
tasks.definition_of_done: Time-series DB (InfluxDB/TimescaleDB) stores pipeline metrics; ingestion handles 400 pipelines at 1-minute granularity; retention policy set to 90 days.

tasks.name: Implement core monitoring API: pipeline status, freshness, lineage endpoints
tasks.definition_of_done: REST API returns pipeline health, data freshness, and lineage; response time < 500ms for single pipeline query; supports filtering by criticality.

tasks.name: Build frontend dashboard: pipeline health overview and lineage visualization
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard displays all 400 pipelines with status; lineage graph renders for any dataset; responsive design; loads in < 3 seconds.

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases
milestones: All three data sources (Airflow, dbt, Snowflake) integrated end-to-end
Lineage cross-system validation complete
Alert routing to on-call system tested
Performance testing at 400-pipeline scale completed
Security review completed

tasks.name: Integrate Airflow, dbt, and Snowflake metadata into unified lineage graph
tasks.definition_of_done: Lineage graph connects Airflow tasks → dbt models → Snowflake tables; tested with 50+ sample pipelines; handles missing lineage gracefully.

tasks.name: Implement SLA breach detection and alert generation logic
tasks.definition_of_done: Alert rules evaluate every 1 minute; SLA breach detected within 5 minutes of occurrence; alert payload includes pipeline name, SLA threshold, and lineage impact.

tasks.name: Integrate alert routing to on-call system (PagerDuty/Opsgenie/internal)
tasks.definition_of_done: Alerts sent to on-call within 2 minutes of SLA breach; on-call engineer receives alert with full context; alert acknowledgment logged.

tasks.name: Handle edge cases: schema drift, missing metadata, stale data, API failures
tasks.definition_of_done: Graceful degradation when Airflow/dbt/Snowflake APIs unavailable; stale data flagged in UI; schema changes detected and logged; no silent failures.

tasks.name: Performance test: dashboard and API response times at 400-pipeline scale
tasks.definition_of_done: Dashboard loads in < 3 seconds; API queries return in < 500ms; lineage graph renders for 100+ node DAGs in < 2 seconds; no memory leaks under sustained load.

tasks.name: Security review: data access controls, API authentication, audit logging
tasks.definition_of_done: Security review completed; RBAC implemented (data engineers see all pipelines, analysts see only relevant datasets); audit log captures all API access; no sensitive data in logs.

phases.name: QA & Testing
milestones: All critical bugs resolved
UAT completed with data engineering team and analysts
Runbooks and operational procedures documented
Monitoring and alerting for platform itself configured

tasks.name: Execute comprehensive test suite: unit, integration, end-to-end
tasks.definition_of_done: All unit tests pass; integration tests cover Airflow/dbt/Snowflake connectors; end-to-end tests validate full pipeline from ingestion to alert; code coverage > 80%.

tasks.name: UAT with data engineering team: validate pipeline detection, alerts, lineage accuracy
tasks.definition_of_done: Data engineers test against 50+ real pipelines; confirm all failures detected within 5 minutes; alerts routed correctly; lineage matches manual inspection.

tasks.name: UAT with analysts and finance: validate self-service data freshness queries
tasks.definition_of_done: Analysts can query data freshness without contacting data engineering; finance confirms board-report datasets are tracked; no support tickets for 'is this data fresh?'

tasks.name: Write operational runbooks: incident response, platform troubleshooting, maintenance procedures
tasks.definition_of_done: Runbooks cover: alert triage, false positive handling, connector failure recovery, database maintenance; reviewed by data engineering team.

tasks.name: Configure monitoring and alerting for platform itself (meta-monitoring)
tasks.definition_of_done: Platform health metrics (API uptime, ingestion lag, alert delivery latency) monitored; alerts fire if platform itself fails; SLA for platform availability set to 99.5%.

phases.name: Deployment & Handoff
milestones: Production deployment completed
Data engineering team trained on platform operations
Documentation published and accessible

tasks.name: Deploy platform to production: database, API, frontend, monitoring
tasks.definition_of_done: All components deployed to production; smoke tests pass; rollback plan tested; on-call rotation configured.

tasks.name: Conduct knowledge transfer and training with data engineering team
tasks.definition_of_done: Data engineering team trained on platform operations, alert triage, and troubleshooting; at least 2 engineers certified as on-call operators.

tasks.name: Publish user documentation, API reference, and operational runbooks
tasks.definition_of_done: Documentation accessible in internal wiki; covers user guide, API reference, runbooks, FAQ; reviewed by data engineering team.

risk_register.description: Airflow 1.10 metadata database has no official API and requires direct DB reads. Schema may be undocumented, unstable, or incompatible with extraction logic. If schema reverse-engineering fails or requires extensive custom handling, Phase 2 development stalls.
risk_register.trigger: Direct DB read queries fail or return unexpected schema; Airflow version upgrade breaks extraction logic; schema contains undocumented tables or columns.
risk_register.mitigation: Complete schema audit and documentation in Phase 1 (T1); test extraction queries against live Airflow instance before Phase 2 begins; establish fallback: if direct reads fail, negotiate with Airflow vendor for supported API or consider Airflow upgrade path.
risk_register.contingency: If schema is incompatible, pivot to Airflow REST API (if available in 1.10) or upgrade Airflow to supported version (adds 3-4 weeks); escalate to VP of Data for timeline adjustment.

risk_register.description: dbt vendor has flagged the internal API used for metadata extraction as deprecated and scheduled for removal in the next major release. If deprecation occurs during Phase 2-3, integration work must pivot to alternative API or workaround.
risk_register.trigger: Vendor announces deprecation timeline < 6 months away; API becomes unavailable during Phase 2-3; vendor releases major version with API removed.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm deprecation timeline and alternative API availability in Phase 1 (T2); document API contract thoroughly; design extraction layer to be API-agnostic (abstract interface); establish relationship with dbt vendor for early notice of changes.
risk_register.contingency: If API is deprecated mid-project, pivot to alternative (dbt Cloud API, manifest parsing, or custom integration); rework Phase 2-3 integration logic (2-3 weeks); escalate to VP of Data for timeline adjustment.

risk_register.description: Data lineage visualization scope is ambiguous. If stakeholders expect column-level lineage (which columns transform into which columns) rather than dataset-level lineage (which datasets feed which pipelines), Phase 2 scope expands significantly and requires data catalog integration.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder feedback in Phase 2 or 3 requests column-level lineage; data catalog integration becomes a requirement; lineage visualization does not meet analyst expectations.
risk_register.mitigation: Define lineage granularity explicitly in Phase 1 (T5); validate with VP of Data and analyst representatives; document scope boundary: dataset-level lineage only, no column-level tracking.
risk_register.contingency: If column-level lineage is required, defer to Phase 2 post-launch; integrate data catalog (Collibra, Alation, or custom) in separate workstream; timeline extends beyond Q3 deadline.

risk_register.description: 20-week timeline is aggressive for a TYPE_C data pipeline project with three external system integrations (Airflow, dbt, Snowflake) and legacy API constraints. If any integration encounters unexpected complexity, critical path slips.
risk_register.trigger: Airflow schema reverse-engineering takes > 1 week; dbt API integration encounters undocumented behavior; Snowflake query performance degrades at 400-pipeline scale; Phase 2 development encounters blocking technical issues.
risk_register.mitigation: Apply 15% schedule buffer (already included in 20-week estimate); front-load Phase 1 discovery to surface integration risks early; allocate 2-3 days per week for integration troubleshooting in Phase 2-3; establish daily standup to catch delays early.
risk_register.contingency: If critical path slips > 1 week, reduce scope: defer lineage visualization to Phase 2 post-launch; defer Snowflake data freshness to Phase 2 post-launch; focus MVP on Airflow + dbt + basic alerting.

risk_register.description: Team is small (7 people) for a 20-week project with high technical complexity. If any critical path role (backend engineer, data engineer) is pulled to other workstreams or becomes unavailable, timeline slips immediately.
risk_register.trigger: Backend engineer or data engineer allocated to production incident; team member takes extended leave; competing project demands shared resources; part-time allocation becomes necessary.
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from VP of Data for full-time team allocation; establish clear escalation path for production incidents (do not pull project team); cross-train frontend engineer on backend tasks to provide backup.
risk_register.contingency: If team member becomes unavailable, hire contractor for 4-6 weeks; escalate to VP of Data for timeline adjustment; reduce scope to MVP (Airflow + dbt only, defer Snowflake).

risk_register.description: Platform will have access to sensitive pipeline metadata and data freshness information. If security review (T18) uncovers missing RBAC, audit logging, or data access controls, Phase 3-4 work must be reworked.
risk_register.trigger: Security review identifies missing authentication, RBAC, or audit logging; data engineers can see analyst-only datasets; sensitive pipeline metadata exposed in logs or API responses.
risk_register.mitigation: Define RBAC model in Phase 1 (T5); implement authentication and audit logging in Phase 2 (T11); conduct security review early in Phase 3 (T18) to allow time for rework.
risk_register.contingency: If security issues are found late, defer non-critical features to Phase 2 post-launch; extend Phase 4 QA timeline by 1 week for security rework.

risk_register.description: Performance at 400-pipeline scale is unvalidated. If dashboard or API response times exceed targets (< 3 seconds for dashboard, < 500ms for API), Phase 3-4 optimization work is required.
risk_register.trigger: Performance testing (T17) shows dashboard load time > 3 seconds; API queries take > 500ms; lineage graph rendering takes > 2 seconds for large DAGs; database queries timeout.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct performance testing early in Phase 3 (T17); use production-scale data (400 pipelines) for testing; identify bottlenecks and optimize before Phase 4 UAT.
risk_register.contingency: If performance issues are found, optimize database queries, add caching, or reduce lineage graph complexity; defer advanced features (full lineage visualization) to Phase 2 post-launch.

risk_register.description: On-call alerting infrastructure (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or internal equivalent) is assumed to exist and be accessible via API. If it does not exist or is not accessible, Phase 3 integration (T15) is blocked.
risk_register.trigger: On-call system does not exist; API access is not available; on-call system requires custom integration not documented; integration takes > 2 weeks.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm on-call system availability and API access in Phase 1 (T2); document integration points; establish relationship with on-call system owner.
risk_register.contingency: If on-call system is not available, build internal alerting system (email, Slack, webhook) as MVP; integrate with PagerDuty/Opsgenie in Phase 2 post-launch.

risk_register.description: This is the team's first project integrating Airflow, dbt, and Snowflake metadata in a unified platform. Technical uncertainty around lineage graph design, metadata consistency, and cross-system integration may surface during Phase 2.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 development encounters unexpected metadata inconsistencies; lineage graph design does not scale to 400 pipelines; cross-system integration requires rework.
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct thorough architecture review in Phase 1 (T3); prototype lineage graph design with sample data before Phase 2; allocate 20% of Phase 2 effort to design rework and iteration.
risk_register.contingency: If design issues surface, extend Phase 2 by 1-2 weeks; defer advanced lineage features to Phase 2 post-launch; focus MVP on basic pipeline health and alerts.

risk_register.description: Frontend engineer is the sole owner of dashboard development (T12). If frontend engineer becomes unavailable, dashboard development is blocked and critical path slips.
risk_register.trigger: Frontend engineer takes leave; frontend engineer is pulled to other project; frontend engineer leaves company; dashboard development encounters blocking technical issues.
risk_register.mitigation: Cross-train backend engineer on frontend stack (React, TypeScript) to provide backup; document dashboard architecture and component design; use component library to reduce custom code.
risk_register.contingency: If frontend engineer becomes unavailable, hire contractor for 4-6 weeks; defer advanced dashboard features (custom filters, export) to Phase 2 post-launch.

open_questions.question: What is the exact deprecation timeline for the dbt internal API? Is it 6+ months away, or sooner? This determines whether Phase 2-3 integration is viable on the current API or requires pivot.
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If deprecation is imminent (< 3 months), Phase 2 integration must pivot to alternative API or workaround; adds 2-3 weeks to critical path and may cause Q3 deadline miss.

open_questions.question: Does the on-call alerting infrastructure (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or internal system) exist and have an accessible API? If not, what is the fallback (email, Slack, webhook)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If on-call system does not exist or is not accessible, Phase 3 integration (T15) is blocked; must build internal alerting system as MVP, adding 1-2 weeks.

open_questions.question: Is data lineage scope limited to dataset-level (which datasets feed which pipelines) or does it include column-level lineage (which columns transform into which columns)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If column-level lineage is required, Phase 2 scope expands by 4-6 weeks; requires data catalog integration (Collibra, Alation, or custom); timeline extends beyond Q3 deadline.

open_questions.question: Can the team be secured for full-time allocation (80%+) on this project for the full 20 weeks, or are there competing priorities that may pull backend engineers or data engineer to other workstreams?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If team members are shared or part-time, critical path slips immediately; timeline extends beyond Q3 deadline. Requires written commitment from VP of Data.

open_questions.question: Who is the Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization and feature trade-offs during Phase 2-3 sprints? Is it the VP of Data, the PM, or a dedicated product owner?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If PO is not named, decision-making delays during Hybrid SDLC sprints; scope creep and timeline slip.

Five assumptions logged (A1-A5) — each represents an unvalidated risk that could extend timeline or require scope reduction
SDLC is Hybrid — requires sprint-based refinement in Phases 2-3, adding execution uncertainty vs. Predictive approach
Small team (7 people) for 20-week project with high technical complexity — resource continuity risk if any critical path role becomes unavailable
Stakeholder sign-off on lineage scope and on-call integration not explicitly confirmed in input — scope ambiguity creates rework risk

scoping_options.tradeoffs: Analysts cannot self-serve data freshness queries in MVP; lineage visualization deferred; requires Phase 2 post-launch workstream.

scoping_options.description: Extend timeline to 22-24 weeks; deliver full scope (Airflow + dbt + Snowflake + lineage) with realistic buffer for integration complexity.
scoping_options.impact: Full scope delivered with 2-3 week schedule buffer; reduces execution risk.

scoping_options.description: Hire contractor backend engineer for 8-10 weeks (Phases 2-3) to accelerate Airflow/dbt/Snowflake integration; keep core team at current size.

scoping_options.tradeoffs: Increases budget by $30,000-$40,000 (contractor cost); requires onboarding time (1 week); contractor may not have domain expertise in Airflow/dbt/Snowflake.
